articles.title: Clavicular’s accuser drops sexual assault claims from civil lawsuit amid MA criminal rape case
articles.summary: A woman who accused “looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular of raping her at his family’s Cape Cod home last May has refiled her civil lawsuit and dropped the sexual assault allegations against him, a move her lawyer said was intended to avoid interfering with a pending Massachusetts criminal case in connection with the encounter.
articles.body: A woman who accused “looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular of raping her at his family’s Cape Cod home last May has refiled her civil lawsuit and dropped the sexual assault allegations against him, a move her lawyer said was intended to avoid interfering with a pending Massachusetts criminal case in connection with the encounter. Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged last month with rape, drugging someone for sexual intercourse, and procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old. He has denied the allegations detailed in the Sept. 8 criminal complaint filed in Orleans District Court in Barnstable County, Massachusetts. Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, an 18-year-old influencer known online as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, alleged that in May 2025, while she was in Massachusetts, Peters called her an Uber to his family’s Cape Cod house. Once there, she said he got her drunk on vodka while they livestreamed on Twitch and then raped her, according to a criminal complaint from the Chatham Police Department. The charges come months after Mendoza filed her original civil lawsuit against Peters in Miami, accusing him of sexual assault in connection with the events of May 2025. The civil lawsuit also separately alleged he injected her face with a non-FDA-approved fat-dissolving substance during a November livestream in Florida. A source familiar with the matter previously confirmed to NBC News that the charges against Peters stem from Mendoza’s allegations. On Thursday, Mendoza filed a second amended civil complaint in Miami-Dade County, Florida, removing the sexual assault allegations against him and scaling back the details of the alleged assault. The civil complaint also details allegations that Peters falsely represented himself as qualified to perform cosmetic injections during a November 2025 encounter, concealed their risks, and misled Mendoza about what was being injected into her face. “In light of Mr. Peters’ recent posts and other conduct, this matter is more appropriate for the criminal justice system,” Mendoza’s lawyer, Drew Moss, said in a statement, noting that the sexual assault claim was dropped “due to the pending criminal charges in Massachusetts.” “Ms. Mendoza does not want her civil case to interfere with that process.” Mendoza’s earlier civil complaint alleged that Peters had sex with her after getting her so intoxicated that she was unable to consent. It also alleged that Mendoza woke up to find Peters having sex with her without her consent. Peters’ arraignment in the Massachusetts criminal case, previously scheduled for Oct. 14, was canceled, according to the case docket. The next hearing date appears to be on Oct. 22. The second civil complaint, however, no longer includes those explicit allegations of nonconsensual sex, instead stating that Peters “had sex with Mendoza multiple times while she was intoxicated.” It also does not include the original claim that Peters had sex with her while she was asleep. Moss did not respond to additional questions about the decision or why an attorney originally on the civil case filed a motion to withdraw on Friday. Peters’ spokesperson declined to comment on Mendoza’s latest civil complaint. The influencer has previously denied the criminal allegations and defended himself in a series of posts on X shortly after the charges were reported. The posts include a video of Mendoza calling Peters “super nice.” Mendoza’s amended civil complaint still accuses Peters of battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, fraudulent misrepresentation, fraudulent concealment, and unauthorized publication of name and likeness. The amended complaint also alleges that in November 2025, Peters invited Mendoza and her friends to his place in Delray Beach, Florida, for a streaming session on Kick after they ran into each other at a networking event in Miami. Mendoza alleged that during the livestream, Peters injected her with a syringe of Aqualyx, a fat-dissolving compound he did not reveal was not approved by the Food and Drug Administration, which he said would reduce fat in her face, without her consent, according to the amended civil complaint. The amended civil complaint also provides more detail about the November 2025 incident, including that Peters allegedly knew Mendoza was a minor when he gave her the injection. It also includes screenshots of livestream viewers’ comments warning Peters that Mendoza was 17 at the time. According to the civil complaint, Peters allegedly responded to comments about her age, defended their two-year age difference, and proceeded with the injections. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at rainn.org/get-help.

articles.title: Shreveport's former Libbey Glass plant left more than 850,000 sq ft of contaminated industrial space; after cleanup, full demolition is moving ahead with about 95% of its steel, brick and concrete set for recycling
articles.summary: Full-scale structural demolition is under way at the former Libbey Glass plant in Shreveport after specialist crews successfully cleared industrial
articles.body: Full-scale structural demolition is under way at the former Libbey Glass plant in Shreveport after specialist crews successfully cleared industrial contaminants across more than 850,000 square feet of floor space. The milestone, announced by the North Louisiana Economic Partnership (NLEP) and reported by KEDM Public Radio and KSLA, removes the primary environmental barrier to redeveloping the 54-acre industrial property at 4302 Jewella Avenue. Known as the I-20 Legacy Site, the location is being prepared to host new commercial and industrial employers along one of North Louisiana's most strategic transport corridors. Work at the site began with targeted abatement activities before expanding into full environmental remediation. With hazardous materials now safely extracted, heavy machinery is moving across the property to dismantle the remaining structural frames and overhead infrastructure.Dismantling prominent local landmarks along Jewella AvenueLocal residents and motorists traveling along Jewella Avenue will soon witness the most visible phase of the project as demolition teams tear down the massive industrial silos that have dominated the skyline for decades. Crews operated by Nabors Demolition LLC initiated preliminary site preparation in April 2026. Following the official confirmation of complete environmental clearance, structural teardowns are accelerating across the entire 850,000-square-foot footprint. Project schedules published by the NLEP show that full demolition and ground-level preparation work will continue through mid-2027. Rather than hauling the demolished structures directly to regional landfills, contractors are sorting and crushing materials directly on-site. According to the NLEP, approximately 95 per cent of all concrete, brick, and structural steel salvaged from the plant will be recycled for future construction projects. This process significantly reduces municipal waste while lowering the overall environmental footprint of the clearing operation.Transforming a historic industrial footprintThe Jewella Avenue complex originally served as a manufacturing plant for glass tableware giant Libbey Glass, which operated at the site for nearly five decades. Operations at the facility ceased at the end of 2020 following corporate bankruptcy restructuring, leaving behind one of the largest vacant industrial properties in Caddo Parish. To prevent the vast complex from deteriorating into a permanent brownfield, the NLEP stepped in to acquire the property in September 2025. By taking direct control of the site, the regional economic development group sought to eliminate environmental liabilities and accelerate the timeline required to bring new manufacturing, logistics, or distribution jobs back to Shreveport. The property features direct rail access and immediate proximity to Interstate 20, making it a prime candidate for heavy industrial or logistics operations once the land is fully cleared and graded.Creating new economic opportunities for North LouisianaEconomic leaders consider the physical cleanup of the property a necessary investment to keep North Louisiana competitive for national and international business expansion projects. In a statement provided to KEDM Public Radio, NLEP President Justyn Dixon explained that converting former industrial plants into development-ready acreage is vital for attracting modern employers who require fast construction schedules. "The work being completed at the I-20 Legacy Site is about more than demolition," Dixon said. "It is about creating opportunity. Every step toward site readiness increases our ability to attract new industry, support existing businesses, and build a stronger economic future for the region." By taking on the risk of environmental remediation and site clearance upfront, local development officials aim to present potential buyers with a pad-ready location free of legacy liabilities.Ongoing coordination and future outlookThe multi-year redevelopment strategy represents a joint effort between regional development authorities, municipal leaders, and state agencies. Support for the initiative includes partnership from the City of Shreveport, Caddo Parish, and regional economic financing partners. As heavy equipment continues to work through the site, local authorities are advising nearby residents to expect continued truck traffic around Jewella Avenue through the completion target in mid-2027. Further announcements regarding potential industrial buyers or tenant recruitments for the I-20 Legacy Site are expected once site clearing approaches its final stages.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cornell suspends fraternity parties after alleged campus gang rape case
articles.summary: Fraternities face immediate emergency suspensions for violations amid sweeping ban tackling parties at US university.
articles.body:
Cornell University has suspended fraternity parties for the academic year and will give the New York State Police a role in investigating sex crimes on campus.

The Ivy League university announced the major changes on Tuesday, as it sought to reassure the rattled campus community amid the ongoing outrage over its handling of allegations that a female student was sexually assaulted at a fraternity house in 2024.

The accusations came to light after the former student, known as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit last month.

In addition to the blanket suspension of all parties and social events at fraternity houses through the 2026-27 school year, Cornell President Michael I Kotlikoff announced a new “zero-tolerance” policy for violations, noting that any fraternity chapter that breaks the ban will face an immediate freeze.

“These measures will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue,” Kotlikoff wrote in a letter addressed to the campus community on Tuesday.

The university president pledged to strengthen Cornell’s sexual misconduct response by adding a dedicated case manager to the Office of Civil Rights to guide survivors through the reporting process.

Kotlikoff affirmed that he will be transferring investigative authority from the university police to independent, trauma-informed investigators with the New York State Police in an effort to reform the handling of sexual abuse cases on campus and restore community trust.

Kotlikoff acknowledged that sexual violence extends beyond fraternities, saying Cornell must also confront a campus culture of excessive drinking and drug use and expand education about students’ responsibility to intervene when others are at risk.

Cornell also plans to add victim advocates and expand sexual violence prevention programmes, including education aimed at encouraging bystanders to intervene, he said, calling the various actions announced Tuesday “first steps toward systemic change on our campus”.

“We will take all necessary steps to address the conditions that led to Jane Doe’s experiences, and those of other survivors,” he said.

Doe’s lawsuit was brought against the Chi Phi fraternity at Cornell University and seven of its members, accusing them of drugging and gang raping her during a party on the night of October 19, 2024.

Following her initial allegations in 2024, Cornell shut down the fraternity and temporarily suspended the accused male students, two of whom were later expelled. But critics have said the university’s response was too lenient, prompting it to launch an independent review into its handling of the case, led by a former top US prosecutor.

“We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action,” Kotlikoff said. “Cornell must be a place where safety is not an open question.”

articles.title: Russia arrests Japanese reporter for alleged espionage
articles.summary: Suspect was arrested on Russia’s far-eastern Sakhalin Island before being transferred to Moscow, says Russia’s FSB.
articles.body:
Russian authorities say they have arrested a Japanese journalist on the far eastern Sakhalin Island, accusing him of espionage.

The Federal Security Service (FSB) announced the arrest on Tuesday, saying the man was believed to have gathered information on Russia’s defence capabilities for Japanese intelligence. The charges carry up to 20 years in prison.

Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs named the journalist as Imai Yuki, who it said worked for Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper.

The Japanese government was trying to verify reports of the journalist’s detention, according to an official at Tokyo’s embassy in Moscow cited by Japan’s Kyodo news agency.

The journalist was arrested on Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, the main city on Sakhalin Island, as he was preparing to leave Russia, said the FSB. He was then flown to Moscow, where a court ordered him to be held behind bars pending the probe, the agency added.

A video shared by Russia’s TASS news agency, attributed to the FSB, shows masked officers appearing to handcuff the suspect in a hotel room, before transporting him to an interrogation room.

The suspect was then shown boarding a plane accompanied by two FSB servicemen, before appearing in a cage on trial in a Moscow court, which authorised his custody for nearly two months.

The Japanese man’s arrest comes amid a spike in tensions between Russia and Japan following Russian President Vladimir Putin’s trip in August to the Kuril Islands , the Moscow-controlled Pacific archipelago that is claimed by both countries.

The Sakhalin region includes Sakhalin Island and the four southernmost islands of the Kuril chain, which Japan calls the Northern Territories.

Russia and Japan never signed a formal World War II peace treaty, with the main obstacle being the ⁠unresolved territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands.

Authorities in Russia have arrested numerous foreigners for alleged espionage since it invaded neighbouring Ukraine in 2022.

One of the most prominent cases was the detention of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich in 2023. He was found guilty of espionage by ‌a ‌Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in a major prisoner swap involving Russia and Western countries in August 2024.

articles.title: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa.
articles.body:
Missiles and drones have been intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says.

Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said several projectiles targeting the Saudi capital and other cities were intercepted after the coalition carried out a strike on the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility on Tuesday night.

The Houthis warned they would target the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam.

Al-Maliki later said missiles targeting cities including Dammam had been intercepted, while shrapnel had fallen in a residential area in Dhahran.

It came as the Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the Iran-backed group would "bear the consequences" of its recent deadly attacks on the kingdom.

Thirteen people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, while another person was killed in a similar attack there the following day.

On Tuesday, the coalition said its forces had destroyed three drones north of Riyadh.

The Houthis have said they are targeting airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones in response to deadly Saudi strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including Sanaa.

The Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces mounting an offensive on Yemen's Red Sea coast and several other front lines.

A correspondent for AFP news agency reported that queues formed at petrol stations in Sanaa on Tuesday afternoon following the coalition's warning of an impending operation against the al-Sabaha oil facility, with many residents worried about shortages.

The Yemen Petroleum Company, which is run by the Houthis, issued a statement that sought to reassure them, saying the facility "does not contain any stock of petroleum products".

The company also said it had "taken all necessary precautionary measures to address any emergency, ensuring the stability of the supply situation and the continued meeting of citizens' needs in a normal manner".

After al-Maliki confirmed the strike, first reported by Houthi media, explosions were heard over Riyadh and other Saudi cities, with al-Maliki reporting four missiles and two drones had been intercepted near the capital.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.

US President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on Tuesday the Houthis were "behaving very badly... and purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices".

Speaking to reporters, he did not answer a question on whether he'd made a decision to help the Saudis retaliate against them, but said he "might" ask Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan to intervene.

Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes.

Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed in Yemen since August. The UN's human rights office says they include at least 54 civilians, half of them children.

More than 216,000 people have also been displaced across the country, and suspected cholera cases have tripled in three weeks, rising from 217 to 647, according to the UN.

articles.title: Major cruise line hikes its popular package prices in move that could hit vacation budgets
articles.summary: Vacationers are reacting as Princess Cruises hikes Plus and Premier package cruise prices by $5 per person per day with major changes to Wi-Fi plans starting Oct. 13.
articles.body: Princess Cruises is increasing prices on some of its most popular add-on packages by $5 per person per day starting Oct. 13 and adjusting the cruise line's Wi-Fi plans. And some cruise fans say they may rethink their vacation plans as a result. Princess Cruises' Plus and Premier packages include drink packages, Wi-Fi, crew appreciation, casual dining and room service. The higher package rates apply to all sailings that depart on or after Oct. 13. CRUISE LINE'S TOUGHER BOOKING RULES IGNITE BACKLASH OVER HIGHER DEPOSITS AND PAYMENTS The Princess Plus package is due to increase to $70 per day, and the Princess Premier package will increase to $105 per day, the company shared with Fox News Digital. Package prices will increase to $75 and $110 on the Sun Princess and Star Princess. "We periodically review package pricing to account for changes in our operating environment while continuing to offer guests strong value and a convenient way to bundle popular amenities," a spokesperson for Princess Cruises told Fox News Digital. "We believe both packages offer strong value, providing guests with a convenient way to bundle popular amenities. CRUISE FEE DOUBLES AT VACATION HOT SPOT AS PASSENGERS BRACE FOR EVEN STEEPER HIKES "Additionally, crew appreciation included in these packages continues to go directly to the hardworking crew members who deliver the exceptional service our guests know and value," the cruise line, based in Santa Clarita, California, added. Princess Cruises' bundled packages outline distinct tiers of shipboard perks. Under the Princess Plus package, guests receive up to 15 alcoholic beverages per day (capped at $15 each), four casual meals, complimentary room service, prepaid gratuities and Wi-Fi coverage for one device per traveler. "We believe both packages offer strong value, providing guests with a convenient way to bundle popular amenities." The top-tier Premier package expands those perks to unlimited drinks valued at up to $20 each, paired with unrestricted casual and specialty dining. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER In addition to included room service and gratuities, Premier guests receive four-device Wi-Fi access and up to $300 per person in shore excursion credits. The cruise line is also restructuring its standalone internet offerings by retiring its four-device Wi-Fi tier, the company said. In its place, Princess has introduced a two-device option priced at $39.99 per day. Purchasing single-device internet access once onboard now costs more as well. Rates have risen to $39.99 per day for a single 24-hour purchase, or $33.99 per day when booked for the entire sailing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES People took to social media to weigh in on the new pricing structure. "They're just making my decision to sail standard and pay à la carte even easier," one Reddit user said. In response, another commenter said, "With inflation, high fuel and food costs, I suspect gratuities, cocktails, specialty dining and coffee, etc. will all go up al la carte, as well." Another person wrote, "Just bought the 4-device internet package for our two upcoming cruises. Just another reason [that] after these cruises we are going to explore other lines." "It’s probably no longer worth it for me." Some people said the higher price could make Princess Plus less worthwhile to them, especially for those who don't use all the benefits. "I think this price increase is what will push me away. … It’s probably no longer worth it for me," one traveler said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Princess Cruises also recently announced it's introducing stricter booking policies, including higher deposits and earlier final payment deadlines. Among the biggest changes is an update to the timeline for final payments, the cruise line confirmed in a previous statement to Fox News Digital. "Beginning with new bookings for sailings departing in 2027 and beyond, we are implementing a 120-day final payment and a modified cancellation fee schedule," the company said in August. "These changes bring greater consistency to the booking process and reflect broader industry practices, while also helping ensure that guests have fair access to the staterooms and sailings they want to experience." The premium line's newest additions are its Sphere Class vessels, Sun Princess and Star Princess. Kelly McGreal of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

articles.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis sentenced to 40 years in connection to Tupac Shakur’s 1996 murder
articles.summary: The man convicted of orchestrating rapper Tupac Shakur’s killing in 1996 has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison.
articles.body: The man convicted of orchestrating rapper Tupac Shakur’s killing in 1996 has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison. The sentence includes a 20-year mandatory enhancement for profiting off the murder, Judge Carli Kierny told the court. “You don’t get to take a man from his family,” she said to Duane “Keffe D” Davis. “You don’t get to take his very life, his whole life, and just walk away from it, especially when that man is Tupac Shakur.” Davis, 63, was found guilty in August of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon. Much of the two-week trial hinged on Davis’ own accounts of the killing in media and in a memoir, which prosecutors said was precipitated by a scuffle between Davis’ nephew and Shakur on the night of his death. “He would have been the promise of our parents. I believe when you take away someone like that, you deserve the maximum sentence,” Shakur’s younger sister Sekyiwa Shakur said during her victim statement Tuesday. She said her brother was “born an icon” and was raised to be a human rights activist and a protector for his family and friends. “He was a father figure to me,” Sekyiwa Shakur aded. “It wasn’t just me in everybody in our immediate family, our extended family, and as we got older, our community as a whole.” It took jurors less than three hours to convict him. On Tuesday, Davis appeared in court shackled in handcuffs and wearing a navy blue prison uniform. When asked if he wanted to address the court, including Shakur’s family, Davis declined. “I’m good,” he said. Pointing to five other convictions and Davis’ public boasting, Clark County Chief Deputy District Attorney Binu Palal asked for the maximum possible sentence. “Whatever your decision is, ultimately, in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence because he’s earned through his actions, his behavior, who he is as he stands here today,” Palal told the judge. “He 100% deserves the maximum possible sentence.” Davis remains the only person convicted in Shakur’s murder. He was not accused of firing the fatal shots, but prosecutors argued he provided the gun and helped orchestrate the attack. His role in Shakur’s assassination in Las Vegas had been at the center of a nearly 30-year mystery that riveted rap fans, true-crime experts and conspiracy theorists. Investigators at the time pointed to an East Coast-West Coast record label rivalry that they said prompted a bloody feud between Shakur’s entourage and Davis’ henchmen. They blamed Shakur, his friends and other associates for stymying their investigation, and failed to connect the dots between known gang leaders, prosecutors said. The case went cold for decades until 2019, when Davis released his memoir “Compton Street Legend.” In it, Davis recounted his involvement in Shakur’s assassination and described himself as a “shotcaller” for the South Side Crips. Their rivals, Mob Piru, was associated with Shakur’s record label and its co-founder, Marion “Suge” Knight. During the trial over the summer, Palal argued that Davis “went hunting” for Shakur and Knight after they were spotted at a Las Vegas hotel beating up Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, known as the “prince” of Compton in California because of his ties to Davis. Knight was in the car with Shakur and was also shot that night. He survived his injuries, but Shakur died six days later. His death sparked a gang war hundreds of miles away in Compton, and was followed by the killing six months later of New York-based rapper Christopher Wallace, also known as Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie. No one was ever charged or convicted in Wallace’s death.

articles.body: A 26-year-old South Dakota sheriff's deputy has died after being shot during a confrontation at a Sioux Falls home that also left a suspect wounded. Minnehaha County Deputy Katherine Frank was critically wounded Friday night when gunfire erupted about 30 minutes after deputies arrived at the home, the Minnehaha County Sheriff's Office said. articles.title: Prepare yourself for a look at a rare albino caribou calf photographed possibly for the first time
articles.summary: A biologist's photos capture an albino caribou calf with red eyes and pink hooves north of Fairbanks, Alaska — the first images of one in nearly 50 years.
articles.body: You want your OutDoors with a story? How about this one? A rare albino caribou calf was photographed recently in Alaska for what very well could be the first time. Jordan Pruszenski, an Alaska Department of Fish and Game biologist, was counting caribou calves in a small plane north of Fairbanks when she spotted a white speck. The late June routine activity to determine how many calves survived their first month was about to become anything but routine. The white speck was a rare albino caribou. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS "I’m just like, 'What is happening'" Pruszenski said, reports KOTZ. "You could totally see it like on the horizon, and then it steps onto like the snow patch and totally disappears." The pilot turned the plane back towards the animal for another look. As the plane took another pass, Pruszenski snapped several photos. In addition to the white fur, this calf also had "incredible, beady red eyes" and pink hooves. This rare sighting came with even rarer photographic evidence. The Alaska Department of Fish and Game's last record of an albino calf was from 1976. It had been observed through a spotting scope for a couple of minutes and no photos were taken. WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA As for this calf, there's no way of knowing if it has survived past the one-month check in late June. Biologists didn't collar the calf or the mother and its white fur is going to make it stand out to predators. "Once it steps off of the snow it just really stands out," Pruszenski said. "So we’re really not sure how long it’ll last." The name of the albino caribou's herd isn't being shared, so that people don't head out on their own looking for it. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "If you happen to see it, it’d be great to let us know. But what we don't really want is people to really be sort of trying to bother this caribou," Pruszenski told the outlet. "We want to be able to give it its best shot, which will be to kind of just let it be a normal caribou." That sounds perfectly reasonable. Let the caribou do caribou stuff. It's not looking for fame. Enjoy the photos of the rare animal and keep it moving.

articles.summary: The man who was killed by a tiger at a zoo in South Yorkshire has been locally identified as William Chapman, a youth in his 20s who managed to enter the
articles.body: The man who was killed by a tiger at a zoo in South Yorkshire has been locally identified as William Chapman, a youth in his 20s who managed to enter the tiger's enclosure. The police have not named him officially. Chapman was seen walking up to a 200kg male Siberian tiger named Attai, who attacked him, and Chapman was pronounced dead at the scene shortly after the attack.Several fake and AI-generated videos of the purported incident went viral and police advised people not to share them. In verified videos. onlookers urged him not to approach the tiger and to "play dead". As an investigation is going into the incident, the Yorkshire Wildlife Park remained closed for the fourth day on Tuesday.Altai is an endangered tiger and he would not be euthanised.No security system could have prevented himAmid questions as to how Chapman could enter the enclosure, experts said it a thied is detemined to enter somebody's house, no security system can prevent that. Dr Campbell Murn, a previous member of the government's zoo expert committee and lecturer at the University of Reading, said while it was a tragic incident, determined people could get inside zoo enclosures."I view it in the same way a determined thief will get into somebody's house or somebody's car and despite the best security systems and enclosures sometimes these things happen," he said.Amy Dickman, a professor of wildlife conservation and the director of WildCRU at the University of Oxford, told Guardian: “I would not conclude that there was a major issue with zoo safety – the harsh reality is that it is virtually impossible for zoos to stop people who are very determined to breach safety measures.”An eyewitness told BBC News that she saw Chapman pacing around with his headphones in by the tiger enclosure. Then she saw him climbing up onto the barriers. When the tiger grabbed him, he was shouting for help. Some people attempted to distract the tiger but people were confused as they did not understand what was going on.Chapman was a former student of the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe. articles.title: Your fave roll, chowmein to pinch pockets this Durga Puja as LPG and kitchen staples bite
articles.summary: Kolkata street-food prices may rise this Durga Puja as vendors face higher input costs, including commercial LPG up to Rs 2,954, costlier onions and eggs.
articles.body: Kolkata: The joy of hopping from one pandal to another through the night, stopping occasionally for an egg roll, a fish fry or a steaming plate of momo is about to become a costlier affair this Durga Puja. Struggling with soaring input prices, street-food vendors are preparing to pass on at least a part of the burden to the customers.In recent weeks, commercial LPG rates have risen by Rs 70 per cylinder, onions have crossed Rs 70 a kg and eggs, sugar and maida have become dearer, weighing heavily on kitchen budgets.The price shock comes just as thousands of temporary food counters prepare to spring up along popular pandal-hopping routes. From Rashbehari Avenue and Gariahat to Esplanade and north Kolkata, vendors who depend on the festive rush say their profit margins are being squeezed even before the celebrations begin.Commercial LPG, indispensable for roadside kitchens, now costs Rs 2,954 for a 19kg cylinder in Kolkata, up from Rs 2,884 in Sept. The revised rate took effect on Oct 1. The increase has coincided with higher prices of several ingredients essential to the city’s street-food economy.“Earlier, we could absorb small increases in the prices of ingredients because Durga Puja brought higher sales. But this time, almost everything has become costlier — cooking gas, onions, eggs, maida and sugar. We can’t continue selling rolls and chowmein at the old rates without compromising our earnings. Customers may have to pay a little more,” said Shankar Rakshit, a fast-food vendor on Rashbehari Avenue.Maida, the principal ingredient in rolls, parathas and several fried snacks, is selling for Rs 38 to Rs 52 a kg in wholesale markets, depending on quality. Rising egg prices have added to the cost of egg rolls, egg chowmein and egg-toast.Sugar, another essential ingredient for tea stalls, sweet shops and bakeries, has also become dearer. Bakers have already raised prices of bread and cake and the inflationary pressure is now spreading to roadside eateries.At Esplanade, where food stalls cater to commuters, shoppers and pandal-hoppers, traders fear a sharp price hike could hurt sales. “Puja is the biggest earning season for many of us. But customers are also price-conscious. If we increase the price of every item, some may buy less. Yet maintaining the old rates is becoming increasingly difficult. We are caught between rising costs and customers’ expectations,” said street-food seller Raghu Pradhan.The squeeze is unlikely to remain confined to makeshift counters. Small restaurants, fast-food outlets and takeaway kitchens that depend on commercial LPG and daily purchases of vegetables, eggs and flour are also vulnerable to the price escalation.For habitual pandal-hoppers, food is as much a part of the festival as the pandals themselves. “We plan our puja outings around food stops. An egg roll here, a plate of chowmein there, followed by tea and sweets — that is part of the excitement. But when every stop becomes more expensive, the combined bill for an entire family can be substantial. articles.title: Horse carriages in New York City expected to be outlawed
articles.summary: Both the speaker of the city council and the mayor have expressed support for ending the practice.
articles.body:
New York City Council is expected to outlaw horse-drawn carriages starting in June 2028, a ban that also has the support of the mayor.

The legislation follows the death of a teenager who fell off a horse-drawn carriage in Central Park this year, and ongoing concerns about inhumane treatment of the horses.

The teenager's death led to Speaker of New York City Council Julie Menin's support of the bill, which she said will come before the council for a vote on 22 October.

"Horse-drawn carriages have long been part of New York City's history, but in an increasingly busy Central Park, this tradition has become a growing public safety liability," Menin said in a statement to the BBC.

"Next week, the Council will take decisive action by voting on [this bill] to protect New Yorkers, visitors, and the horses themselves."

The bill - called Romanch's law for the teenager who died - has support from a council majority, a spokesperson for the speaker said.

A Mamdani official said the mayor, who also supports banning the industry, is constructing a plan to transition those in the horse-drawn carriage business.

"We have been working closely with the City Council, union partners, carriage drivers, animal welfare advocates, and community leaders to deliver a just transition that protects workers while ending horse-drawn carriages in Central Park once and for all," a spokesperson said.

The latest version of the legislation includes an "industry transition framework" including potential job placement, training, career counseling, and financial compensation for those involved in the business. The bill does not allow the horses to be sold for slaughter or for the same purpose.

It is not the first time officials have pushed to end the industry, which is a longtime New York tourist attraction. Former New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio announced soon after his inauguration in 2014 that he wanted to ban the carriages in Central Park, citing poor treatment of the horses, and proposed a fleet of vintage electric cars to replace them.

In the end, he implemented new rules restricting where carriages can pick up tourists.

In June, Romanch Mahajan, who was visiting New York from India, was riding in a carriage when the horse pulling it bolted, causing the 18-year-old to fall and die.

His father, Deepak, later told the city council he could not "properly describe to you the real, true fear inside that carriage".

Also this year, a carriage horse named Dennis died in Central Park from eating a toxic plant.

Some workers' groups, including the Transport Workers Union - which says it represents 300 horse-carriage drivers and owners - have pushed back against legislation banning the industry. The Transport Workers Union argues the horses are treated well and that the industry employs hundreds of people.

Last year, the Central Park Conservancy, the nonprofit group that manages the park, said it was supporting legislation to ban the practice.

"We do not take this position lightly," the conservancy's president, wrote in a letter, "but with visitation to the park growing to record levels, we feel strongly that banning horse carriages has become a matter of public health and safety for park visitors".

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s nephew responds to restraining order, denies threatening violence
articles.summary: Dolly Parton’s nephew denied accusations that he threatened to use violence and destroy his aunt’s legacy, telling the court the messages were taken out of context from a specific business dispute, according to a new court filing.
articles.body: Dolly Parton’s nephew denied accusations that he threatened to use violence and destroy his aunt’s legacy, telling the court the messages were taken out of context from a specific business dispute, according to a new court filing. Bryan Seaver submitted an affidavit on Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, in response to a temporary restraining order request by She’s Alive, the entity that manages and protects Parton’s professional property and business. The company had accused Seaver last month of sending increasingly threatening messages and describing himself as an “international arms dealer” as part of the threats. According to Seaver, the situation arose from a dispute between his security company and the company that operates Dolly’s hotel and museum in downtown Nashville. Seaver’s company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, provided security for the hotel and was owed approximately $251,000 in services rendered, the affidavit said. “SAPS had not been paid since approximately one to two weeks before Ms. Parton died on August 25, 2026,” Seaver said. All invoices from Seaver prior to Parton’s death were sent to Danny Nozell, Parton’s longtime manager who runs She’s Alive, he said in the affidavit. The messages referred to in the restraining order were sent directly to Nozell, Seaver said. Seaver said in his affidavit that the messages were “sent in the course of private conversations between two friends” and that they were never sent to employees of She’s Alive, referred to as “SAL” in the filing. “I have never threatened physical harm to Mr. Nozell, to any SAL employee, contractor, attorney, advisor, or business partner, or to anyone else associated with SAL,” Seaver said. “I have no intention of doing so.” Seaver describes his messages to Nozell regarding the alleged threat to ruin Parton’s legacy as part of his frustration at not being paid by the company managing her hotel, Herschend Family Entertainment. He said the podcast conversation was part of a larger discussion on the large number of media requests Seaver received following his aunt’s death, which Nozell was advising him on. The message from Seaver read, “I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f------ pay me.” “They were not a threat made to SAL or any third party. Mr. Nozell never replied that I should not do it or that it was a bad idea,” Seaver said in the affidavit. Seaver also included screenshots of messages in which he references being an international arms dealer in his filing. Part of Seaver’s security work involves working as an arms broker between the U.S. government and the Haitian National Police, he clarified in the affidavit. The screenshots in Seaver’s filing include a purported reply from Nozell to the message saying, “You should promote that.” The messages appear to be in the context of the numerous media requests Seaver has received following Parton’s death. Seaver also wrote, “I just sold 29 million dollars worth of ammo to Haiti. I’m not exactly a media person, Danny,” according to the filing. Other messages from Seaver included in his filing appear to express a desire to cut the Herschend Family Entertainment out of Parton’s business dealings. Seaver wrote that he would “ratf--- every Herschend entity I can possibly conjure.” A spokesperson for Herschend Family Entertainment did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Seaver admitted in his affidavit that his language was crude, but said he understood the “slang” to mean “undercut or outmaneuver someone in business or politics.” “It does not mean physical harm, and I did not intend it that way,” Seaver’s affidavit said. “I have never sent anything to Dollywood or HFE threatening to harm their brand or their personnel.” Seaver also denied allegations made in court that he attempted to avoid being served legal paperwork in this case by putting barbed wire at his front door and caution tape at his home. He said that the request for barbed wire was actually made by his teenage son while Seaver was working. “People repeatedly came to our front door, rang the doorbell, knocked, and pulled on the screen door, beginning early in the morning and continuing during the day,” Seaver said. “The media is constantly at my home.” The barbed wire and tape were put in the home by Seaver’s son and the purpose was to protect the family “from unwanted approaches, not to evade service of process,” the affidavit said. Seaver’s company has since received the more than $250,000 payment and has been replaced as the security company employed by She’s Alive, according to the affidavit. In Seaver’s opposition to the restraining order issued earlier this month, he notes that the restrictions are overly broad. The terms say that he cannot have contact or be within 1,000 feet of anyone who “has or may have” a business relationship with She’s Alive. “I have no way of knowing who all of those people and entities are,” Seaver said. “I could violate the Order without knowing it simply by going about my business in Nashville.” He also noted that this would likely include his own family members, as his mother, sisters, aunts and cousins have employment or connections to Parton’s estate. “A restriction extending to everyone who ‘has or may have’ a business relationship with SAL could reach ordinary communications with close family members,” Seaver said.

articles.title: Trump rally protester attacked in act of ‘senseless’ political violence, Ohio mayor says
articles.summary: At least two men attending President Donald Trump’s rally in Ohio attacked a female protester in a “senseless” confrontation decried by the mayor of Youngstown on Tuesday.
articles.body: At least two men attending President Donald Trump’s rally in Ohio attacked a female protester in a “senseless” confrontation decried by the mayor of Youngstown on Tuesday. A pair of males, one in an adjustable baseball cap and a bald man in a dark t-shirt, put hands on a woman Monday during the GOP event inside Covelli Centre in Youngstown, multiple videos of the incident showed. The man in a blue baseball cap pawed at the woman, wearing a shirt reading “Release the Epstein Files,” and pushed her down before the balding man jumped on her. He appeared to throw multiple punches at the woman’s face, pull her hair and put the victim in a headlock before uniformed law enforcement arrived to take the protester away. “It must be emphatically stated that senseless (political) violence has absolutely NO place in our community or in our democratic process,” Youngstown Mayor Derrick McDowell said in a statement on Tuesday afternoon. “Regardless of someone’s political affiliation or their point of view, every person attending a public event has the right to do so without fear of being assaulted or threatened,” he wrote. “I condemn this senseless conduct unequivocally.” Youngstown police were not at this event, as security was provided by the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office and the United States Secret Service, according to the mayor. It wasn’t immediately clear if anyone was arrested or charged in connection to the incident. Representatives for the sheriff and the Mahoning County Prosecutor’s Office could not be immediately reached for comment by NBC News on Tuesday. The violence briefly delayed Trump’s speech as he watched the assault unfold. He mocked the protester’s weight and said, without evidence, that the woman must have been paid to be there. “You know they’re paid protesters,” Trump said. “That’s a very low class protester.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The president as in Ohio seeking to boost GOP hopes in what has been a reliably red state. Sen. Jon Husted has been trailing in polls against Democratic former Sen. Sherrod Brown and one-time Trump rival Vivek Ramaswamy is also locked in a close battle for the governor’s office against Democrat Amy Acton.
